class.name: ScenarioEventImplementation
class.brief_description: The behaviour of a [ScenarioEventServer] event system.
class.description: What the events of a scenario mean beyond their delay, condition and action - which may not be queued, when one runs, what follows its run - and its own entries in the server's queue ([method ScenarioEventServer.system_schedule]). The server is the dispatcher; the original's event system, its memory cells and launchers, is one implementation. Implement it in C++ by overriding the virtual methods, or in GDScript by overriding the methods below. Every callback carries the system: a Resource is shared by default, so one implementation may serve several systems and keeps whatever state it needs per system RID. An implementation changes the events only through the [ScenarioEventServer] API.

method.name: _event_can_queue
method.description: Whether the system's [param event] may be queued now by [param activator]; it may by default.

method.name: _event_get_run_time
method.description: The simulation time the system's [param event] runs at, queued by [param activator] at [param now]: by default [param run_time], now with the event's delays.

method.name: _event_ran
method.description: The system's [param event] ran, its action done.

method.name: _scheduled
method.description: The time the implementation scheduled [param owner] for ([method ScenarioEventServer.system_schedule]) came; [param ticket] is what [method ScenarioEventServer.system_schedule] returned.

method.name: _system_attached
method.description: The implementation was attached to [param system].

method.name: _system_detached
method.description: The implementation was detached from [param system]; it lets go of everything it kept for it.
